title: Determine optimal circular-cylinder geometry
action: Use an RCWA solver to sweep w/p from 0.2 to 0.4 at a low p/λ (e.g., 0.1) and normal incidence. Identify the w/p that yields a reflection phase closest to 180°. Use this optimal w/p in subsequent steps.
description: Find the width-to-period ratio that gives a constant reflection phase of 180°.

title: Frequency sweep of reflection phase for optimal grating
action: For the optimal circular-cylinder grating found in step 1, compute the reflection coefficient phase at normal incidence for p/λ values 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40. Save the results to /app/outputs/frequency_sweep.csv.
description: Reflection phase vs normalized period for the optimal grating, demonstrating frequency independence.
output_schema: columns: p_lambda (float), reflection_phase_deg (float). One row per p/λ value.

title: Angular sweep of reflection phase for optimal grating
action: For the same optimal grating, compute the reflection coefficient phase at fixed p/λ = 0.2 for incidence angles 0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°, 80°. Save the results to /app/outputs/angular_sweep.csv.
description: Reflection phase vs incidence angle for the optimal grating at a fixed frequency, demonstrating angular independence.
output_schema: columns: incidence_angle_deg (float), reflection_phase_deg (float). One row per angle.
